subject: Re: CCPA/CPRA addendum — service provider language and subprocessor onboarding
messages:
From: Julia Park <julia.park@acmehealth.com>
To: sofia_ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Benson <michael.benson@acmehealth.com>, legal@acmehealth.com
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: CCPA/CPRA addendum and subprocessor list for onboarding

Sofia —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our procurement and privacy teams are ready to move forward but need a couple items clarified before we can sign: specifically, the CCPA/CPRA addendum language that treats Redwood as a "service provider" and the process/timing for subprocessor onboarding and notice. A few concrete asks from Acme legal: 1) confirm Redwood's permanent commitment that Redwood will not "sell" Personal Information as defined under CCPA; 2) provide the current roster of subprocessors and a cadence for notice prior to onboarding new ones (we typically ask for 30 days notice for high-risk subprocessors); 3) clarify whether cross-state data flows (e.g., between CA and NY facilities) trigger any additional contractual obligations in the addendum; 4) provide SOC 2 Type II evidence and a redline of your proposed addendum.

I've attached our standard DPA template with a few comments; happy to take Redwood's redlines as well. Can you confirm timing? Acme needs signed terms before year-end for this pilot.

Thanks,
Julia Park
Senior Counsel — Privacy
Acme Health

Attachments: Acme_DPA_redline_v1.docx

From: sofia_ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Julia Park <julia.park@acmehealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: CCPA/CPRA addendum and subprocessor list for onboarding

Julia —

Appreciate the clear asks and the template. High-level answers up front: 1) Redwood confirms it acts as a "service provider" under CCPA/CPRA and will not "sell" Personal Information; we will include explicit non-sale language in the addendum. 2) I've attached our current subprocessor roster and proposed notice cadence (30 days for new high-impact subprocessors; 7 days for low-impact tooling). 3) We treat cross-state routing of requests/processing as operational transfer only — it does not change our service-provider obligations, but we can add language clarifying the limited-use and data transfer boundaries you asked about. 4) SOC 2 Type II summary is attached for initial review — we can provide the full report under NDA if you need the auditor letter.

Next steps: we'll produce a redline of your DPA and a companion addendum that maps the CCPA/CPRA clauses to Redwood's operational controls. Can we target Tuesday (2026-12-15) EOD PST for a redline? Also looping in Karthis (builds infra policy) and Monica (CS lead on onboarding) to address any integration/ops questions.

Sofia Ivanova
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: subprocessor_roster_2026-12.csv, SOC2-typeII-summary.pdf

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: sofia_ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 14:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: CCPA/CPRA addendum and subprocessor list for onboarding

Sofia/Monica —

Quick technical notes to include in our redline so we don't get pushback from Acme on ops: - For KV/cache and prefix caching we can document retention windows and per-tenant deletion procedures; propose adding a 30-day maximum for cached telemetry unless customer requests otherwise. - For subprocessors: CloudRegional (ops@cloudregional.com) handles host-level infra; our model-ops partner (not public-facing) should be treated as a high-impact subprocessor and we should proactively offer a security questionnaire and 30-day notice. - Cross-state routing: our runtime may route to the nearest available region for latency; we'll add a clause that we will not re-identify or combine data for ad-hoc analytics across accounts without explicit consent.

Also propose we offer a one-time expedited onboarding SLA for high-impact subprocessors when a customer has stricter rules (e.g., Acme wants 14-day notice). That can be a checkbox in the addendum.

Karthik
Director, Platform Security
Redwood Inference

From: Julia Park <julia.park@acmehealth.com>
To: sofia_ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@acmehealth.com, Michael Benson <michael.benson@acmehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 09:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: CCPA/CPRA addendum and subprocessor list for onboarding

Sofia —

Thanks for the prompt reply and the roster. A few follow-ups from Acme Legal after reviewing the roster and your notes: - We appreciate the non-sale commitment; please make it explicit in the addendum (we usually use: "Supplier shall not sell Personal Information, as defined by CCPA/CPRA, and shall process Personal Information only as a Service Provider on behalf of Acme"). - The roster lists CloudRegional — can you confirm whether CloudRegional subcontracts any processing to other third parties? We need the upstream subprocessor map for anything that has access to decrypted data. - For cross-state routing: Acme's privacy team needs a sentence that processing across US states will be solely for operational availability and performance and will not constitute a new use or sale. - Finally, please provide a proposed timeline for when we can exchange redlines and when Redwood can provide the full SOC 2 report under the mutual NDA. Year-end is tight for us; if Redwood can provide a redline by EOD 12/15 and SOC2 under NDA by 12/17 we can likely close.

Best,
Julia

From: sofia_ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Julia Park <julia.park@acmehealth.com>, legal@acmehealth.com
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 16:48:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: CCPA/CPRA addendum and subprocessor list for onboarding — Redwood redlines and next steps

Julia —

Attached are: 1) Redwood's redline to Acme_DPA_redline_v1.docx (tracked changes), 2) a short companion addendum that includes the explicit non-sale clause you suggested and a cross-state routing sentence, and 3) an updated subprocessor roster that highlights high-impact processors and upstream subcontractors. Key commitments in our redline: - Non-sale clause: explicit, permanent (no recharacterization) commitment that Redwood will not sell Customer Personal Information and will act only as a Service Provider for CCPA/CPRA purposes. - Subprocessor notice: default 30-day notice for high-impact subprocessors, 7 days for tooling; we include an expedited 14-day onboarding option if Acme requires it (checkbox in Exhibit). - Upstream subcontractor transparency: we will provide a downstream/upstream map for any subprocessor that touches decrypted customer data; CloudRegional confirms no further subcontracting for decrypted data. - SOC 2: we can provide the full auditor report under NDA by 2026-12-17; summary is already in your packet. - Deletion & retention: per-tenant deletion API + contractual 45-day maximum residual retention for telemetry; we documented steps and proof points in Annex B.

If this looks good, next steps: 1) confirm whether Acme wants the expedited 14-day subprocessor onboarding option; 2) we can prepare DocuSign packet for the addendum and DPA redline for signature; 3) SOC2 under NDA will be transmitted on 12/17.

I'll leave final negotiation language to legal, but wanted to make sure we hit your year-end timeline.

Regards,
Sofia Ivanova
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_redline_to_Acme_DPA.docx, Redwood_CCPA-CPRA_Addendum.pdf, subprocessor_roster_2026-12_v2.csv
